lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: dilation, center, and scale factor

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Dilate (3, −2) about the origin by factor 4.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 4 becomes a side of length 12. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 8; the area is multiplied by 9

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 51° and ∠B = 79°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 51° and ∠E = 79°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away

items.prompt: Dilate the point (5, -6) about the origin with scale factor 5. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 21 becomes a side of length 63. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 42; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 28°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 53° and ∠E = 28°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (3, 7) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
